utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today is Tuesday, the 30th of June, 2009. I would like to welcome all the people present, Mr. Praljak, Mr. Stojic, Mr. Petkovic, Mr. Pusic, as well as all Defence counsel, Mr. Stringer and his team. I would also like to welcome all the people assisting us. The Trial Chamber would like to recall that pursuant to what we said yesterday, Mr. Stojic's Defence will have 45 minutes of extra time, which means, Ms. Nozica, that you have one hour and 45 minutes left to finish. I'll give you the floor right away, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We should now have in front of us binder number 2 for the benefit of the Trial Chamber too. His Honour Judge Antonetti, on the 22nd of June, asked you about the obligations that unit commanders had in relation to the identification of perpetrators of crimes, and that's recorded at page 41790 and 41791 of our transcript. He showed you Article 27 of the Decree on District Military Courts, and let me just indicate the numbers of the documents. That's document P592 and 4D1317.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: Could all microphones that are not in use please be switched off.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This article determines the obligations of company commanders or commanders at higher levels in the chain of command, and now I would like to show you some documents that confirm what you stated regarding Article 27 when His Honour Judge Antonetti asked you some questions. Mr. Praljak, I fully accepted what you said, that you didn't really concern yourself with regulations, that you knew about them in general, and that is why I have several documents that are nothing but regulations at the beginning of the binder. So please skip three documents and go to P00092. That's the fourth document in your binder. Perhaps it will be difficult to find this document because the first three are really very thick documents, and you can just flip them over. The document that I am -- that I need, P92, is the fourth document. Could I please ask the usher to assist Mr. Praljak to find P92, because I can see that we have it in e-court. It should be the fourth document in binder number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: No, P92.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So this is the instruction about the jurisdiction of the commanders in the HVO Central Bosnia Operational Zone with a description of the tasks that pertain to some establishment posts. We see that the year is 1992, and at the first page or, rather, the next page of the document, it is indicated that pursuant to the order on the establishment of the Central Bosnia Operational Zone and in order to ensure that -- its proper functioning, prompt exercise of command over certain formations, Mr. Tihomir Blaskic promulgates this regulation on the internal organisation of the work of the command of the HVO Central Bosnia Operational Zone, with the description of the tasks that the staff are to perform. Could you please go to page 5. It's page 5 both in the English and the Croatian versions, and it stipulates what the obligations are of the OZ, Operational Zone commanders. All the duties are listed here, and under 7 it says -- we're dealing with Article 27 of the Decree on District Military Courts. Let me just bring this to your attention, where it says takes care of the improvement of discipline and order and takes measures against those who commit crimes, and deals with disciplinary infractions and mistakes. It is indicated on the basis of the fact that this pertains -- this is based on the instruction to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he takes care of the improvement of discipline and takes measures against those who commit crimes, once, of course, the name of the perpetrator of a crime is known.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So, in essence, it is true that a criminal report can be filed when one has a name, but now let's see how one gets to the name. Could you now look at the next document. That's P1359. This is an order signed by Mr. Siljeg, and he says here, on the basis of the order of the chief of the Main Staff, dated the 19th of January, 1993 -- for the transcript, I will say that this order has been exhibited and it is P1344. I didn't think that it was necessary for me to show it, so it's 1344, yes. And it is stated as follows: "Gentlemen, soldiers, non-commissioned officers and officers of the HVO, you have to prevent all acts that are not in line with international law of war." And then he goes on to say: "We're not Chetniks, we're not a gang. We are --" the 30th of January, 1993, and I am referring to item 13, item 13, or, rather, 12 and 13 of this order. That's on the next page, where Mr. Siljeg orders to SIS organs, saying they will put together a plan for the elimination of the acts that run contrary to this order and the rules of conduct, and together with the military police, they will continually implement those measures. In item 13, it is stated that the SIS and the military police will arrest any looters and bring them into custody, confiscate and make a record of the stolen goods, and will oppose any resistance to the implementation of this order. Mr. Praljak, this is quite logical, in fact. It's one of the measures that were supposed to be forwarded down the chain of command because it had come from higher up, and this order, issued by Commander Siljeg to the SIS and military police, it's quite logical in terms of fighting crime?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's obvious that the chief of the Main Staff issued an order. At that time, it was General Petkovic, and it is quite clear that it was after Vakuf, the 30th of January. It's probably related to what happened in Vakuf, a bit before that. And it's logical that he orders that SIS organs should perform their duties, and also the military police. So you have to make a distinction between issuing orders to SIS and ordering the SIS and the military police to do their job.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, since you now drew this distinction between exercising command over SIS and ordering SIS to do something, now I want to ask you whether that formation, so from battalion up to brigade and to the operational zone, so did all those units have assistance for SIS in their command structure?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part formations did have assistance for SIS, and the brigade commander or the commander of the given unit exercises command over them. But now we have to make a distinction. He can only order them to do their job in accordance with the regulations, because they have their job, their tasks, that are stipulated by relevant regulations. And when the brigade commander sees that some things do not work, then he tells them, Please go ahead and do your job.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. So you agree with me that this is what Mr. Siljeg is doing, he's ordering them to do their job?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. The same topic, the same commander; the document is P1491. This is again HV -- or, rather, MB. Mr. Praljak, this is an order issued by Mr. Siljeg. He's mentioning the HV Brigade. It's not the Croatian Army; it's Hrvoje Vukcic-Hrvatinic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And "MB" would be a mortar battery; right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, in the preamble of this document, it's exhibited, so I won't stick to it. It says that some soldiers stole items from Muslim and Croat houses, furniture and cattle. You spoke about it, didn't you, that such things happened and that they stole from Croat and Muslim houses alike?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They didn't really mind who the house belonged to as they went about looting.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Siljeg is ordering, in item number 1 -- well, it's irrelevant. But in item 2, he says the brigade commander, together with the security organ, shall immediately come to the Dobrosa village and will examine the status in the battery, examine the facts, and immediately take appropriate measures, pursuant to regulations on military discipline within his authority, and shall recommend appropriate measures to the higher command. Is this command completely logical?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a good order. He says the brigade commander and the SIS, which is duty-bound to carry out an investigation and learn about the facts, if this was not done by the brigade commander, then there is an investigation to be carried out. This is a good order, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's be very clear, Mr. Praljak. He says to the brigade commander, together with the security organ from the brigade; wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm now going to show you one of your documents, which is 3D596. It's the next one in your binder, Mr. Praljak. This is another order, this time by Mr. Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Nozica. I think, really, you go a bit too fast. If you look at page 7, line 7 and following, you say: "Let's be very clear, Mr. Praljak. He says to the brigade commander, together with the security organ for the brigade; wouldn't that be correct?" Probably you said something about what he said to the brigade commander, because as it stands here, the sentence makes no sense to me, at least.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The sentence makes sense, both in English and in Croatian. Let me repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That means that the brigade commander must do that together with the security organ from the brigade, together? So together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Now it's a complete sentence. But what is here is not a complete sentence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you very much, Your Honour. I apologise. Perhaps I have a problem. Can somebody check whether it's too hot in this courtroom? I can barely stand because of the heat, and if that is indeed the case, then perhaps something might be done about it. But maybe it's my problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you ask the technicians to lower the heating, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, so now I've called up 3D596. You found it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is an order by Mr. Obradovic, and in this order he again, in item 1, orders that any looting or any other form of theft of personal or other property of citizens in "our" area of responsibility should be prevented. The perpetrators should be arrested, and proceedings should be instituted against them through this command. In item 3 of this order, again, he says: "Immediately prevent all violent behaviour and any war crimes by members of the 1st Brigade, and any units attached to it, and other persons who happen to be in the area of responsibility of the brigade. All violent offenders shall be disarmed, and proceedings shall be instituted against them through this command." I assume, Mr. Praljak, that you consider that this was fully in line with Mr. Obradovic's powers, in particular because you chose this document as a document that you wanted to comment on.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true, I did see this order, I'm familiar with it. It's the 3rd of July. It's obviously after the 30th of June, in his area of responsibility. There was high treason in the HVO ranks. Members of the Croatian Defence Council were killed in the rear, not in combat, in an ambush. And I don't know who gave him unlimited authority in the preamble. Well, I don't know what this is all about. But in item 6, for instance, he says the commanders, in their areas of responsibility, must not allow any searches or detention of people bypassing the military police and the SIS. So he notes here that the military police and the SIS are the organs who are in the brigade charged with conducting searches and detaining people if any crimes are detected.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That's correct, and this is their job in the brigade. They are charged with that task in the brigade, among other things, and he spells it out; the military police and the SIS of the brigade. So it is uncontroversial. And indeed he's submitting this document, among other addressees, the chief of the SIS of the Knez Domagoj 1st Brigade of the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's not writing to the chief of the brigade SIS, or perhaps he's writing to the chief of the SIS, the person who is in charge of all the people in the SIS. So you really have to be -- well, he would probably have put the brigade SIS chief -- chief. Perhaps he's also addressing this to the chief of the SIS, the person who is in charge of the SIS. So there's a collision here. The SIS is a structure which is attached to brigades to assist. There's the assistant to the brigade commander, but that person is independent in the conduct of his duties and his job, in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. Let us move on to the next document. That's the third document, so skip two documents. It's a 3D document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If you allow me, Ms. Nozica, my attention was drawn to number 7 in this order, which says: "Group the Muslim population in your zone of responsibility and secure them with your men." Mr. Praljak, are you aware of any cases where this was actually done? And if so, could you tell us about the example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't comment upon this, Your Honours. This was on the 3rd of July, and I arrived later. I can only assume that because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. No offence intended, but I'm not interested in your assumptions, because we also, of course, can make assumptions. You said you were not there at the moment. Is this an order for one day, or for one week, or is it an order which one would think that it would be valid until replaced by another order or until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 24th of July, I arrived and assumed duties as the commander, which means I was not in that area on the 3rd of July. I was in Boksevica. I remember I was there as a foot soldier. As far as this order is concerned, they were issued at the moment when a high treason happened in the area. Around that time, 26 soldiers of the HVO were massacred in the rear, behind the lines, in Capljina -- or, rather, near Capljina. And at that time, you couldn't know who the soldiers were and who the civilians were because all the civilians were armed. And I suppose that for security reasons, this order was issued with a temporary effect in order to prevent further killings outside of the area of combat or behind the lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, you said that you didn't know who the chief of the SIS was and who the order was issued to. Let's now look at bullet point 11, which encompasses everything that we've said, and it says: "All the unit commanders shall be responsible to me personally for the execution of the order." And under 12: "In case the order is not carried out and if measures are not taken in keeping with the order, the unit commanders will be punished under the law." Does it arise from this that Obradovic believes that all his subordinates shall be considered responsible for the main execution of this order?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Nozica, there's several bullet points in this order, and not every bullet point applies to everybody. This means that the commanders must not search and bring people in, but they have to make sure what their soldiers are doing. Orders have to be obeyed and carried out. However, one order is carried out by his commanders and the rest of them are carried out by his assistants, the SIS, the logistics, and so on and so forth. Everybody is responsible for one of the bullet points in the order, is what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, if that is the case, are we talking about the individuals who are subordinated to the unit commanders?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are coming back to the unit commanders and the subordinates. Hold on, Ms. Nozica. Let's once and for all deal with that. A unit commander has his assistants, an assistant for the IPD, an assistant for the SIS, an assistant for the military police. In some of the elements, they are subordinated to the commander. If the commander says, We are going to a field mission or do some reconnoitering in a certain area, then they have to obey, but they have their own respective tasks. For example, a doctor has his tasks. A commander can ask for a change, he could issue a proposal, but he could not appoint that person. There is a SIS structure headed by the chief of the SIS, and the SIS chief was the one who approved the appointment and supervises the work of those people. This is the segment appointment. I'm afraid that we're talking at cross-purposes, in which you interpret command, orders, and subordination in one way, and I know that your way is not good.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, allow me, please. I have a lot of documents that I wanted to show you. I wanted to show how things looked in practice. It really doesn't matter whether my interpretation is good or whether yours is good. I am interested in what things looked like in practice. I told you that at the very beginning. We started talking about who issues commands to whom. Whether of two of us are talking at cross-purposes, I don't think that we are talking at cross-purposes. I'm just showing you documents that may be contrary to your interpretation. I'm kindly going to ask you to go through the documents with me. Yesterday, Mr. Praljak, we saw, when it comes to the SIS and the IPD, that the commanders of the brigades issued proposals and that it didn't go, as you say, through the SIS Administration or the IPD Sector. But let's look at the document together, and then we will either agree or agree to disagree. It is not my objective at any cost for the two of us to agree.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just respond. A proposal to appoint somebody is not the appointment. The proposal is a proposal; an appointment is an appointment. Whoever appoints may be -- dissolve the person of his duties, and this is the responsibility and this is the structure that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, yesterday we saw some examples of proposals for the dissolution of tasks, did we not?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we now look at the following document, which is 3D1189. This is also another one of your documents, issued by Mr. Harah. The period is August, and the order is about the frequent occurrences of smuggling and other acts of crime, and this order goes very precisely into the details as to who is supposed to do what. Under bullet points 6 and 7, it says that: "Any willful behaviour on the part of the soldiers, or seizure of goods from individuals, with a view to achieving material again should be strictly sanctioned and disciplined and, if necessary, criminal proceedings should be started." And again under bullet point 7: "In case this order is not carried out or is not carried out consistently, I shall hold the commanders of companies and battalions personally responsible." This is very similar to the orders that we saw previously; am I right, Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is here calling for some order among his units.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I believe that we are now going to the next document, which is 2D3011. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We are now talking about the SIS and the relationship between the assistant SIS of the operation zone and the commander of the operation zone. The date on the document is the 25th of May, 1993, and Mr. Ante Sliskovic, the deputy commander of the Central Bosnia Operational Zone in Vitez, submits to the commander of the operational zone, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, the following information, and he says: "Here enclosed please find information about the events in the village of Ahmici in Vitez municipality. This information is based on the operative information and statements provided by the witnesses of these events as well as the inspection of the site. "The information is not complete because we could not obtain information from all the key witnesses." Further on, it says: "We also did not take statements from individuals of Muslim ethnic origin who fled after the incident in Ahmici ..." And it also says: "Once the combat activities are over and once the favourable conditions are in place, we shall take all necessary measures to elucidate these events." It says here "Annex 1." This is a Prosecutor's document, because you can see the ERN number, but we could not locate the annex that was supposed to attach to it. In the same light, could you please look at the following document, and then I will put my question to you. The topic is still the same. The number is P4268. This is an order issued by Mr. Blaskic and sent to Mr. Sliskovic on the 17th of August, 1993, and it says "Continuation of Investigation into the Killings in Ahmici Village." And it says: "In order to establish the facts and undertake measures in order to carry out investigation, on the event of the killing of civilians in Ahmici," he says, "Continue together and record data on the deaths of civilians in Ahmici in order that the whole of the material be collated and presented to the competent organs of the District Military Court." Under 2 is details of operations, and under 3 it says: "The deadline for the execution of this order is 17th September, 1993, when you are to submit a completed report to me so that it may be forwarded to competent organs for further action." Mr. Praljak --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down, especially when reading a document. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, according to your information, and one dates from the period when you were there, I'm not going to ask you whether you know about this specific event. Do they reflect the relationship between the commander of the operation zone and his assistant for SIS, in the operation of SIS, whereby he issues him with orders and the assistant reports back to him?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Both documents are very clear. The commander says to the organ that is in charge for the investigation to carry out the investigation. And in addition to submitting material to him, he should also submit material to the District Military Court and all the competent organs. And this is the complete clarity. The commander of the brigade or the operational zone has an assistant who -- in the organisation who assists him with the investigation of crimes. This is the SIS, which also encompasses the military police. Either in keeping with or not keeping with these two things have the duty to -- listen, look, for example, you come somewhere where a crime took place. There is no criminal there, of course, the perpetrator is not there. It will take weeks or months to investigate the matter, or I don't know how long, because whoever committed the crime is in hiding. And there are two services in place in charge of collecting material evidence of carrying out crime investigation procedure. And to do everything that is necessary and that the military police was in charge of doing, they had the Crime Investigation Services. The commander is duty-bound to issue them with orders to do what they're supposed to do, and that's that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, that's that.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And just in passing, even if he had not issued the order, it was their duty to do what they're supposed to do. But it's neither here nor there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, just very briefly, let's go to the following document in light of what you have just told me. The number is P6846. Mr. Lasic -- I intentionally wanted to show you this to show the practice, and I took a stroll along the time and the space. The number is correct. And now Mr. Lasic, as you can see, Mr. Lasic is referring to the order of the Main Staff and says, under 1: "Urgently analyse the criminal acts committed in your units. Engage the SIS organs in these tasks as a priority." There is a spelling mistake in the original, but I believe that I'm reading it well. This is beyond the time and space -- you were not in the HZ-HB, and Mr. Stojic was also not there, but this illustrates the work of the commander?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He says, Go to the military police and engage the SIS in order to elucidate the matter. And this is very clear. The Main Staff is trying once again -- the brigade commander is once again trying to put an end to whatever he has information about, and then he obviously turns to two things for assistance, and these two things are the SIS and the military police, and it's very logical.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I have a very strict Judge here who's my co-counsel at the same time, and he will not allow me to speed. And he says under bullet point 7, he says the persons in charge are commanders of certain units and assistants for commanders for SIS?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. They have to cooperate. It's clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, we have only two or three more documents left about this document -- about this topic, and the following document is 4D517.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It is the 24th October 1993. We've already spoken about this investigation. This investigation was carried out by the Prosecutor, but these are just inspection activities that preceded the investigation. And here Mr. Blaskic sends his order to Mr. Rajic, the 2nd Operative Group commander in Vares, and he says that he should initiate an investigation against Mr. Zvonko Duznovic, an assistant for Security and Information Service in the Bobovac Brigade. The investigation shall be conducted in accordance with Article 107 of the Rules of Procedure and Military Discipline. And he also says that the officers from the brigade command should be used to carry out the investigation or the officers of the Operative Group 2. Just one more document which is very closely connected to this, which is 4D855, and this will bring us to the end of this topic. And now we see that Mr. Rajic submits the order to the chief of the SIS of the OG-2 and says as follows: "Conduct investigative proceedings against Zvonko Duznovic, assistant for SIS in the brigade Bobovac, on grounds of reasonable suspicion." And says under 3: "During the investigative proceedings achieve full cooperation with the members of the command of the brigade and with other relevant persons who are familiar with the activities of the aforementioned official." Mr. Praljak, these two orders show the chain. Mr. Blaskic issued his order to Mr. Rajic, and Mr. Rajic, in his turn, issued an order to his assistant for SIS for conducting investigative proceedings?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for conducting investigative proceedings. It was their right and duty to carry out an investigative proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Of course, we must not ignore the fact that the true investigation is carried out by the prosecutor who is duty-bound to do that. That's why I started with the Law on Criminal Proceedings, but we don't have to go through that. And, finally, the last document that you very often mention in your examination-in-chief, which is 4D834 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down. It's almost impossible to follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Madam Nozica, again to interrupt you, but it is already the third time today that the interpreter is asking you that, Would the counsel be so kind to slow down. And I would only like to repeat it to you and, of course, also to Mr. Praljak, the same request, and it is the umpteenth time that we are doing this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. My colleague keeps warning me to slow down because he's following the transcript, but I suppose Mr. Praljak and I, because we speak the same language, seem to run away with ourselves and don't wait for the end of an answer before my question begins. But I'll do my best to improve in future.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Anyway, Mr. Praljak, you've spoken about this document several times so far?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The last day of my work, I signed it where Mr. Petkovic's name is, and I require a summary report about Stupni Do and that investigative proceedings be taken against Kresimir Bozic. So that is the information that we had at that time as to who could be guilty, the guilty party.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you to take up the third binder, which will be the last binder that we're going to deal with. Yes, that's right, that's the first document in binder number 3. Mr. Praljak, let me just make a short introduction. We have document P6203 in front of us now, and you were asked about this document during the examination-in-chief; in fact, on two occasions. Judge Antonetti asked you about it, and you gave your answers on the 8th of June, and it is on pages of the transcript 39001 to 39003. And this same document was shown to Witness Ivan Bagaric on the 21st of April, 2009. And now I do apologise. The pages I stated just now relate to Mr. Bagaric's examination and testimony, not yours. Now, let me just remind you of what you said about this document, and this is something that Mr. Bagaric confirmed; that he did not have the right to command. And in this document, it says that: "We do not have the necessary institutions and individuals." And for that reason, he considered that this order should be placed adapta [as interpreted]. Now I'm going to show you the next document, which is 2D717, and this is a letter from Mr. Siljeg of the same date. And he says that: "The order of the Health Sector with respect to the detainees of the detention centre and Centres for Preventive Isolation should not be considered compulsory, it should be declared null and void, because centres like this do not exist here, and even if they did, they are not under our jurisdiction. Our concern is only the battle-field." So Mr. Siljeg sent this out to all the subordinate brigades, he sent this order out to all of them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Praljak, Mr. Bagaric, according to you, was not in a position to command Mr. Siljeg. And according to Mr. Siljeg, he could not have commanded the brigade within this operation zone either; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he couldn't. Right on both counts.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, when we come to the Medical Corps, and it is P3286, that's the document number, let's try and answer two questions now using that document. Did centres, as they're called here, for detainees, detainee centres and Centres for Preventive Isolation exist, because that is something that Mr. Siljeg claims in this paper? And you said that as far as you knew, they did not exist. Now, let's just see if we agree as to what the chain of command was. And the next document is P3286. So this is the head of the Rama Brigade. The date is the 7th of July, 1993. And he says: "On the basis of the situation at present in the Rama-Prozor municipality, and securing health control for the Muslims found in the building of the secondary school centre," and issues an order to the Medical Corps to ensure that doctors visit the facility where the Muslims are in detention. And he says the head of the Medical Corps, Budimir, is in charge. Now, I know, Mr. Praljak, that you, on the 7th of July, did not occupy that post, that is to say, you weren't commander of the Main Staff at the time. However, let me ask you whether you ever had any knowledge that, nonetheless, certain persons were detained in the area which Mr. Siljeg commanded, let's say, in July, and that when he wrote this previous order, he ought to have known that detainees did exist in this area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who took the Muslims into custody. Siljeg does not say that they were not detained. What he says is that they were not under his responsibility and authority. And, secondly, in this document, P3286, I mean, the fact that Marinko Zelenika is ordering a physician to examine the Muslims that were detained, that's his right and duty. It's the duty of the doctor there to do that. He can't ask for a doctor to come in from the Health Sector in Mostar. That's impossible. It is the duty of the physician, and the duty of the commander, once he learnt that there was a need for this, to tell the doctor to go and see what the need was. But from that, it does not arise that he was in charge and had authority over the location where the detained Muslims were.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Praljak, I find this a bit difficult to explain. A commander is in charge or not. If he's in charge, he can dispatch representatives of his services, such as Medical Service, and give them a task. But if he's not in charge, how does he, nevertheless, engage his means, his military means, for something that he's not competent or not in charge? It does not -- it is not in line, at least, with my own experience, as far as command and military structures and so are concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot, Judge Trechsel, enter into your structures and where you were, but it is a physician's duty to provide assistance everywhere. When he's -- if he's a civilian, if somebody loses consciousness, faints on the road, even if he's not his house doctor, he has to help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, this is not the situation of the good samaritan, nor a person of medical training who sees need for action, but it is a commander who commands someone who is under his orders to do something in an area which he says, It's none of my business. He seems to split what he likes to do. He says, I do it. And what he -- he doesn't want to take responsibility. He says, I wash my hands, I have nothing to do with it. Isn't it a bit contradictory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, none at all. There's no doctor -- if there's one doctor in the brigade, then your interpretation is based on the assumption that doctors do exist, that there were doctors, as much as needed in every service. No, there weren't. We didn't have them. In that area, Zelenika saw that there was no doctor, and so he told the doctor to go over there and offer his assistance, but that does -- it does not follow that the person to whom that assistance is given, that he's responsible for that. Wouldn't it be worse if he says, It's nothing to do with me, so don't give any medical assistance? There's no logic there. So I would do the same thing that Zelenika did, I would act the same way. I would help, whether it was under my command or within in my remit or authority or whatever, especially within structures that are in no way organised as they are in the Swiss Army. So the principle was: Do what you can, when you can, when needed, if there's no better solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I leave it at that. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I went back to these documents because on several occasions, at least on two, as far as I remember, during the examination-in-chief, you said -- or, rather, you confirmed that what Mr. Siljeg said was true and correct; that is to say, that there were no centres like that and there were no people of that kind in his area. And a document was shown to you, which we'll look at in just a moment, where Luka Markesic, the chief, talks about taking Muslims into custody on the basis of an order from a higher level. Now I'd like to show you that order, which is already an exhibit. Perhaps you've never heard of that order and it wasn't there when you were there, but let's just agree whether this is the higher level. And it is P3234 that I'd like you to look at now. The document goes to explain some of the questions that you were just asked by Judge Trechsel. Have you found the order? Yes, you have; right. So this is the 6th of July, that's the date, and as I say, you didn't know about this because it was before your arrival. But, anyway, it is Mr. Siljeg commanding here and stating that all Muslim men aged between 16 and 60 are arrested and detained, and he says the military police and the SIS of the Rama Brigade shall be held responsible for carrying out the order. And: "The order shall take effect immediately," it says. And let me emphasise that it is already an exhibit. It has been shown several times. Let me just ask you: Is that a higher level, and did you have no knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge at all about this. At that time, as far as I remember, I was at Boksevica, and I cannot say whether or not this higher level applies to Siljeg. It says what it says, it speaks for itself, and I can't offer any further comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Praljak, let's look at several other documents. We're going to skip one, two, three -- five documents. Let's skip five documents, and when we come to -- and now we come to P3971. They're all short documents, so perhaps you could look at them on your screen. There we are, that's the document that was shown to you, where Mr. Luka Markesic, from the Security and Information Service of the Rama Brigade, is sending out this report to the Presidency of the HVO and the command of the Rama Brigade, and says that the Security and Information Service and military police acted according to an order from a higher level. And we saw that Mr. Siljeg was issuing an order to this effect, that they carry this out, that the SIS and military police of the Rama Brigade carry that out. And then he's asking that a selection be made, and that's the document that you were shown; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was shown it. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now I'd like to show you another document. Let's skip the documents in between and go to your own document which you signed. It is P4260 and it is your -- well, I just wanted us to clarify one point. This document was sent by packet link. There's no doubt about that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, we don't have your signature. We see, up on the stamp, "Received by packet communications," so that's how I know that. Now, somebody, in handwriting, wrote "SIS," S-I-S, and then "sent to BP Rama." Now, I'm interested to know whether you wrote that addition on to the document, and if not do you know who might have entered that onto this document?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not my handwriting, and I don't know whose it is and who wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But we can see that that's what it says?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you didn't send this document out to the SIS of the brigade or any other SIS, did you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: There are three addressees. It says "To," and then we have three listed.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what's your question? What do you want me to answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'll repeat my question. Is it true that you didn't send this document to the SIS of the brigade or the SIS Administration because there are three addressees listed to where it went?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't send it on, but if it says who the addressees are, then I assume that the order would have been sent on. When it reached the Rama Brigade, for example, then it also reaches the SIS of the Rama Brigade, the assistant, of course. But I'm afraid, Ms. Nozica, that between this order of the 6th of July, Siljeg's order, and this one here, dated the 5th of August, I'm not quite sure -- it's too long a period of time for this order to relate to the higher one, to Siljeg's order. I think it's too long a period; that is to say, that Markesic would have written one month later that there was an order from a higher instance, and he would say, Pursuant to Siljeg's order if it was. He would have no reason not to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I don't know what you're actually saying. Was there another order on detention or are you questioning whether Siljeg sent out this order at all?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not questioning whether Siljeg sent it, because the order exists, so I suppose he did. But all I am challenging is that during the space of a month, something else might have happened, and that is that there was a fresh order from a higher instance to detain the Muslims again. That's possible, because as I say, it's rather a long period of time, too long, in fact, for Markesic to be writing about what happened a month ago, for instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I have not quite understood. Is this your document? Did you write this, the order, not the addition in handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but we weren't referring to that document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Good. In number 1, you order that all prisoners be withdrawn from the tasks they have been given. What does that mean, Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me answer that question once again, then. The previous day, on the 16th of August, and we saw the document which Tolj received, and he was the chief of the Main Staff, he received a piece of information to the effect that prisoners were being taken away to dig trenches, and he told me that. And after that, I issued two orders myself; one for this area, the area where I was, and another one, a general one, a general order applying to the whole of the HVO. And I'm afraid I don't seem to have that, but there is clear proof and evidence on the basis of statements that it does exist. Not that they were not allowed to take them out to dig trenches, but that they were not allowed to take them out anywhere, that the prisoners of war should not be touched at all, and that is -- this is the third time that I'm giving my answer. And so on the basis of information provided by Tolj, I issued this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Praljak, there is a rule, which I don't know whether it is also familiar to you. It is also referred to as the three Cs: command, control, correct. It means that if you give an order, you then have to control whether it's actually carried out, and, if necessary, correct the implementation of the order. Now, is this familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can you tell the Chamber what you did to control the implementation of this order of yours?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Mr. Praljak. I hope to help everybody out, but let's look at the next document in the binder, P4285, which is the information. I do apologise, Your Honour, for intervening, but I think we'll move ahead faster if we look at this document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It may exceptionally be acceptable. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps it's not a bad idea to correct the transcript and say exactly what Judge asked the question, because it says Judge Antonetti and it should read Judge Trechsel on line 16. Just to put that slip right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm glad that there is opportunity for you to correct with regard to me also. It gives more equality.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I am sure I would do that far more often and notice things like that if I didn't have to look at the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Anyway, Mr. Praljak, this is the commander, and he is responding to you with respect to your order; the brigade commander, I mean. Right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He says that it was acted upon.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Praljak, I'd just like to tell you, with respect to the comment you made as to whether another order existed or not between Mr. Siljeg's order and the information sent out by Mr. Markesic, and it is -- you say you don't know whether there was one, so that comment of yours -- on the basis of that comment of yours, can I conclude that at the time you did not know whether there was any order at all, because -- about the detention of Muslims between the ages of 16 and 60?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know about any such order at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us move on to our next topic, and I will complete my cross-examination with two more topics. And one of them is the functioning of the IPD and the SIS, and let us move on to the functioning of the IPD. I will now ask you to look at the document that you, yourself -- well, which was shown to you. That's 3D01206, 1206. You have it in e-court, but I would be very glad if you could find it because then --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I actually skipped just one document there, Mr. Praljak, and I moved on to 1206. Oh, I'm sorry, I'm sorry. Quite a few of them, quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, quite a few of them, because I don't have enough time to deal with all of them. I won't be able to cover everything that I planned. Could I please ask the usher to assist Mr. Praljak, because we skipped quite a few documents. And I do apologise to everyone in the courtroom. I really can't deal with all of it. I was a bit too ambitious in my preparations. 1206.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't find this document, although I'm quite quick when it comes to finding documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, well, you have it -- well, it's been put in the binder, but could you please then look at the screen, and then we'll go looking for it. I would kindly ask, Mr. Usher -- yes, okay, you found it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's binder number 3?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a document that we've already talked about. In the course of your direct examination, you did. It was sent by the assistant commander for IPD, Petar Kalinic, from the command of the Operational Zone North-Western Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: He informs the -- actually, it's addressed to the HVO Main Staff, attention Veso Vegar, but I'm asking you whether this is sent to the Main Staff too. Could you please look at the next page?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Praljak, when it comes to the functioning of the IPD, I have the same question as I did for the SIS. The commanders, from the level of battalion up to the brigade and operational zone, and even at company level, have within -- did they have, within their commands, assistants for IPD, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And those assistants for IPD that existed there in the commands of the units, were they subordinate to the unit commander?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Subordinated in what sense, Ms. Nozica? What does it mean, to be subordinate, subordination? Well, everybody had too few people, but what does it mean, subordinate? Please tell me. Ask me, What does it mean to be subordinate?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you what "subordinate" is, but I'm going to ask you a direct question. Did they receive their orders from the commander of the unit that they were part of, and were they duty-bound to obey those orders?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not have to obey them. They received orders that pertained to the military part; in other words, Let's go out and -- in the field. But they did not receive any orders pertaining to their work, because their work was regulated by other regulations. Well, I was in the IPD in the Croatian Army, and this was all copy-pasted there. So this kind of order, this kind of exercise of command, is not of this sort. It's a parallel system. The assistant -- the brigade commander exercises command over his battalion commanders, and these are his assistants. Just like a mayor of a town has fire-fighters who take care of fighting fires, he tells them or informs them about the fire, and they go out and put it out, and the police. So the exercise of command over them is limited. An action is being prepared. They give their recommendations and proposals. So this is cooperation within the scope of strictly-regulated activities and spheres that those people have. A doctor has to do his job, but he cannot refuse to go out on the battle-field if his brigade or battalion where he's in goes out to the battle-field. So the exercise of command is somewhat different from -- well, those people did their job properly. Most of them really worked hard. But let me just make myself clear here.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I'm asking you very specifically. Did the assistant commander for IPD in the units -- were they issued or could they have been issued orders by Mr. Veso Vegar, who was the chief for the IPD in the appropriate sector in the Department of Defence? Could they have -- could he have issued orders to them as to what to do?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It was his duty to tell them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. Just a moment, then. How could then Mr. Bagaric find himself in a situation where -- Mr. Bagaric, because we've seen the document where Mr. Zeljko Siljeg, and I'm going to tell you this is 2D717, where he sends to all the brigades and says, Well, the chief of the Medical Corps cannot issue any orders to you? How come now that the chief of the IPD can issue orders, and did you ever see any orders issued by the IPD chief to the assistants, commanders in brigades for IPD? Did you ever see any such orders, or the SIS chief to have issued any such orders, or the IPD chief, apart from the professional instructions as to how they should do their job?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- well, such orders did not reach me. But if they didn't issue orders of that kind, then they didn't do their job properly. So it is a duty of the IPD officer, and that was my duty in Zagreb, to issue orders and to organise seminars for the Red Cross, to organise seminars about the political situation, to disseminate information about the developments in Geneva, to instruct the people to go and to see how the wounded would be taken care of, to make sure that they are visited in their wards.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's fine, Mr. Praljak. You told us quite clearly that the commander cannot command.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me what you said. The commander --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander can command him within the framework of operational use. So he can order him to go out in the field with him, to remain there 20 days, and to do his job there. That was what the commander of a company, battalion, or a brigade could do. It was his duty. But it was then his duty to do the job in accordance with the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, well, that's how it was with all the assistant commanders?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, it's a little bit different, or I understand it differently, but maybe it's up to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to object to this question, because I feel that a link is here trying to be established between two situations that are essentially quite different.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The speakers are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the Court to instruct my colleague not to explain various situations in the course of my cross, because she can do that the moment my cross-examination is ended, because this is obstructing my work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will withdraw. I will be asking this in my cross-examination. But here are two different situations which are now being painted as being the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody need intervene, because I know perfectly well how the Defence Department, the brigades and areas functioned, the zones functioned. I know perfectly well what military commands are and what the duties of the military police, the SIS and others are, and any attempt by any lawyer to change my opinion is futile, absurd and incorrect. The duties of people who belonged to the part as it was organised was the same as in Croatia. I was in IPD, and I exercised command over the IPD, and that's how it was done down there. Let me just complete --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course all parties are trying their best to cover a lot of ground in very limited time. Now, that being the case, I would ask that of course my learned friend's objection be sustained and we get back to her questioning. We don't need comment or speeches from any witness, even somebody as distinguished as General Praljak. So perhaps my learned friend can continue with her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, please answer Ms. Nozica's question. Ms. Nozica is representing Mr. Stojic. Mr. Stojic was head of the Defence Department and minister of defence. In the way we understand the defence system, Ms. Nozica wishes to highlight the fact that the SIS operatives and the IPD reported to the brigade commanders, and they were subordinated to the brigade commanders. Therefore, the minister of defence has got nothing to do with all this; i.e., in the SIS and the IPD. This is the case Ms. Nozica is putting and developing. So she's putting questions to you on this topic. Ms. Alaburic is representing her client, and you may wait for the cross-examination to put your question. I was about to say something, but I was waiting for the right time to intervene. Let me take the case of the officer who's in charge of the IPD; information, propaganda, training, and so on. When this person is in a brigade, can the brigade commander call him and say, You are an officer, but I would like you to train the soldiers in the field of the Geneva Conventions, because I believe there is a shortfall in this area. The IPD officer then turns around and says, I will obey your orders, or he will turn around to the brigade commander and say, I must first of all refer to the Defence Department to see whether I'm entitled to do this. Let me give you another example. Let's assume that the brigade commander tells the IPD officer the following: There's been an attack by the BiH. I don't have enough men on the ground. Please pick up your rifle and go on the front-line, execute the order. Does the IPD officer then say, I disagree, I need to refer to the Defence Department and Mr. Stojic and ask him whether I'm entitled to do this? So I've given you two concrete examples. What do you have to say to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second case that you've just presented, Your Honour Judge Antonetti, this case says clearly that the brigade commander, or a commander at any level, cannot, irrespective of the situation, issue an order to his assistant for IPD to take a rifle and go to the battle-field. He cannot do that to his assistant for IPD, SIS, or any other assistant. He can issue orders only to his foot-soldiers. And the first case that you mentioned, he can request and bring booklets containing the Geneva Conventions, but likewise he cannot replace his assistant if that assistant says, No, I'm not going to do it at this moment, I'm first going to consult my chief who is affiliated with the Defence Department. And in that, the brigade commander can file a complaint in which he's going to say, This is what I asked, he refused to do it. And then this complaint will be forwarded all the way up to me, for example, and then I would request for Mr. Stojic to see how come that person in question refused to do a very logical thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, you have a great deal of knowledge, and you have seen how the foreign armies operated; the Warsaw Pact and so on. As far as you know, did things happen this way elsewhere or was this specific to the HVO or to the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Militaries of Eastern ideology did not function in the same way. Western militaries do function in that way. We copied the way particularly of Western militaries, which do not have a high number of professionals; for example, Germany, Italy, and so on and so forth. And in those countries, the Ministry of Defence and its elements -- the Ministry of Defence is separated from the purely military part, and it provides support, assistance to the Main Staff, i.e., to the military in everything; information, investigations, the military police, and so on and so forth. Therefore, just like the Medical Corps, all that is not affiliated with the Main Staff. In Croatia, we tried to organise things in the same way as everywhere else and involve the civilian hospitals to have the highest number of doctors as possible. They were not necessarily soldiers, just like the IPD personnel were not necessarily soldiers. They could be civilians. This is how one tries to de-militarise, well, here you have it, and reduce the possibility or the room for a commander to have too much power. That was the case in Eastern countries, where the military commander was given the possibility to investigate, as the SIS does, to punish as the military police does, and this gave him too much power. And in Croatia, there was a lot of debate about that between those people who joined the Croatian Army from the JNA and those of us who never served in the JNA. And Franjo Tudjman said that clearly and loudly, that he was inclined to organise the Ministry of Defence and the army or model the two after the Western example. And I'm talking about the modular system; You do your job, and when you need assistance, according to the model, people in charge will assist you. But that has a special structure, a special manner of screening the staff, a special way of appointing staff, it has its chief, and everything that is described as things that need to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, what you are saying makes sense, and one can understand what you are saying, but there is a difference. In Western armies, if I take the case of the French Army, for instance, an officer who is in charge of propaganda, well, his corps commander can tell him, Go and hand out leaflets in the village controlled by the enemy so that the soldiers desert, and he's going to execute the order. He's not going to ask the Ministry of Defence what he needs to do. Your IPD operative, who may be a civilian, according to what you are saying, well, he can be independent from the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, it's largely independent from the brigade commander or the corps commander even in the French Army. But it is true that in its parts -- in some parts, he is being used. As an IPD officer in the ministry, I provided support by way of providing information and everything else to the commanders. But I was also independent, and I could dissolve them of their duties, to appoint new ones. They performed the control of the brigade commanders, they had control, and they provided parallel reports about the behaviour of certain commanders, and so on and so form. We're talking about parallel systems here. Likewise, when a unit returns from combat, in the French Legion, then they are examined by a psychologist. The commander says that in his view, a certain soldier had been exposed to too much stress. Whether he is going to be given a leave of absence, or whether he will be treated in the barracks, or whether he will be transferred somewhere else for treatment is up to the psychologist. They examine him, talk to him, and then they say, I know it for a fact this lad has undergone a great deal of shock and he stays. And this is not what the commander of the brigade decides. It's the parallel service that decides that. In other words, services are used. In military terms, for example, we go for a field mission or release false information, release information that we are using a lot of food or that there is more of us than there are, it's the commander who does that, but he has a lot of -- as the SIS, for example, the SIS goes with the brigade, but the essence of the matter is this: You don't find somebody who committed a crime or perpetrated a crime where you heard that crimes were perpetrated, but then the investigation, the conversations with people, and then these people have their own informers within the brigade who are going to convey to them the fact that they had heard that people had gotten drunk and then they had information, that's how you learn who the perpetrators are. Your Honours, after Mi Lai -- - or eight months lapsed before the American Army learned what actually happened. I believe that even more time lapsed than when they heard about prisoners. It is the organs in charge of the investigation who investigate such matters, and that takes time. It takes a lot of time. The worse the system, the longer it takes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at the time. I think it's time for the break, but my colleague here wishes to ask a question first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, a while ago there was a hypothesis that a chief of service, I will call him, for instance, IPD, was ordered or asked by his commander to do something which was within the realm of that order and refuses, and then you said there are complaints. The commander cannot sanction him, but he can complain up to yourself, you said, to the highest commander. Now, I am a bit surprised, because now we are dealing with a specific specialty represented by this person, and I had thought I'd understood that this hierarchy finally ended with the Defence Department and not with the military supreme command. Could you clarify this matter briefly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The top of the chain of command for a SIS member, of a military policeman, or an IPD officer is in the Defence Department, not in the Main Staff. For example, if he refuses to carry out an order, it is not the brigade commander who can remove him. He doesn't have that power, because he did not appoint him in the first place. He cannot -– he can launch an investigation and request investigative measures and proceedings to be instituted, but he cannot remove that person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's why I was surprised when you said that the complaint could come to you. Perhaps I'm sort of misunderstanding. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is now time for the break. We shall stop for 20 minutes. Forty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Ms. Nozica, as I already said, you now have 40 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I would like to come back to some parts of your answers provided to -- in answer to Judge Antonetti's answers [as interpreted] and your explanation about the position of the assistant commander for the SIS and IPD, and the obligations of the sector -- or, rather, the Administration for IPD and the SIS Administration. Mr. Praljak, based on the documents that we have seen, the responsibility for the on-site investigation, and I'm using this word "on-site investigation," not "inspection," because I make a distinction between the two, the investigation carried out by the prosecutor and the on-site inspection which has to be carried out after a crime was committed. In answer to Judge Antonetti's question about the different systems, about the different military systems, you said that the on-site investigations were the job of the SIS in the HVO. Mr. Praljak, the documents we've seen speak to the contrary. First of all, Article 27 of the Decree on District Military Courts charges the brigade commander with that responsibility, and this is entirely confirmed by two documents. In order to avoid searching for them and going back, we're going to see them in e-court, yet once again. We've already seen these documents that show that on-site inspection was the responsibility of the commander and his subordinate assistants. The first document is 2D3011. You can rely on e-court rather than on the hard copy of the documents. This is information provided by the assistant commander for SIS of the Operational Zone Central Bosnia in Vitez, and submitted to the commander of the operational zone, Tihomir Blaskic. And the information is about the events in the village of Ahmici. You confirmed yourself that this was a logical chain of communication. The second document is P4268. This document, speaking about the same event, an order for on-site inspection, is given by the commander of the operational zone, Mr. Blaskic, to his assistant for SIS, Mr. Ante Sliskovic. His order is for Mr. Sliskovic to carry out on-site inspection. It arise from these two documents, and there are more than those, that the on-site inspection is carried out by the commander with his assistants in the unit. Would you agree with me that this is what we can conclude, based on the documents that we've just seen?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with your explanation, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. We shall not take it any further. I'm going to ask you to be very brief in your answers. We won't take this any further because it is your legitimate right not to agree with me. Secondly, you said that the assistant commander in the unit for IPD was a civilian?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I apologise. I misunderstood you, in that case. In that case, would you please go on and explain?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that in the Croatian Army, it could have also been a civilian. I didn't say anything about the HVO. He did not have to be a civilian. He could be a civilian serving in the military, and he could serve for a certain period of time or be assigned to a particular task.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, in a unit such as a brigade, could the assistant commander of that unit, any assistant in any area of work, could he be a civilian at all? I'm talking about the assistant commander -- I'm talking about the assistant commander for any area of responsibility, the SIS, the PZ, the intelligence.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no such cases in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. You are saying that the assistant for IPD in any of units could not be a civilian. Mr. Praljak, I would now kindly ask you, in follow-up to Judge Antonetti's questions about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Nozica. I wonder whether you correctly sum up what Mr. Praljak said. He was asked whether there were any civilians, and he said that there were no such cases. He did not say that it was not possible that he could not be a civilian, if I understand correctly. So perhaps one should ask Mr. Praljak: In theory, would it have been possible that a civilian acts as assistant for IPD in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know of any such cases in the HVO, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I restricted myself and said that in the Croatian Army, for some limited scopes of work, publication of books or broadcast of some films, I used a civilian -- civilians, but I did not transform them, as it were, into military personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I seem to understand that you simply do not know whether, in theory, it would have been possible in the HVO to have a civilian as assistant for IPD.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, do you know, and Mr. Vegar testified about that, that the assistant head of Department for Defence for IPD was a civilian?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let me just remind you that he was, indeed, a civilian. But let's now look at another document, which is P872. If we first looked at the previous document, which was 3D, then if you skip the next one, and then we have P872. It's an order from Mr. Lasic, and he was the commander of the Operations Zone of South-East Herzegovina, and relates to command of the IPD structures in the units. And he says: "There is an everyday phenomenon that our soldiers spend their time off in populated areas wearing uniforms and armed. They go into cafes, behave in a non-military way, and cause incidents among themselves and with civilians. Many of them under the influence of drink, alcohol, resort to fire-arms, destroy facilities, conduct robberies, and use vehicles with HVO insignia, without any control or authorisation." So I think that that goes along the lines of what Judge Antonetti asked you about. Anyway, here Mr. Lasic is issuing an order to all commanders and assistants for IPD, Information and Propaganda, that they are obliged to intensify their work with the men, pointing out possible tragic consequences of such behaviour on the part of individuals and groups. That's point 1 of that order. Now, the last point of that order says that: "The commanders of the units are duty-bound to inform me about the implementation of this order in their regular reports." Now, Mr. Praljak, is that the kind of order that you said were orders that commanders could issue to their assistants and lower-down units? Is this one such order which shows what their authority and scope was?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lasic here is issuing an order to everybody, telling them to do their work properly, because the assistants for IPD and the commanders weren't doing their job. So parallel systems were introduced because of control, and "control" is the key word here. Now, why -- if I might be allowed to explain about this parallel system.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: No, we won't go into that now. I want to show what the situation was de facto. But if you're talking about parallel control, then let's see whether from this order that we have in front of us here, we see anywhere that it was sent to the IPD Sector and the assistant head of IPD, for him to be able to exercise that control, as you say. We can see who it was addressed to, and we see that it was not sent to either the Defence Department or the IPD Sector?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't, and he had to exercise control.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The next order from Mr. Lasic is dated the 22nd of April, 1993. It is P2030, from the previous year -- the first one was from the end of the previous year. This one is from April 1993. It is also an exhibit, and it's an order, and I'm sure you'll remember that on the 22nd of April, it related to putting up the HVO soldiers in the barracks and so on, and this was on the basis of an agreement by which HVO members were to be put up.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could all the microphones be switched off, please, that aren't in use. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, I'm interested in point 9, where it says: "The assistant commander of the Operation Zone of South-Eastern Herzegovina for IPD shall organise meetings with the units and inform them of their duties and obligations stemming from this order, and the meaning of this order and similar orders for the future are life in these territories."
